SMTO-UI-0061 — SMTO couldn't confirm this save came from your page

GUID: 13b0e4d4-a9d9-5596-a476-2841bd8a847d
Slug: csrf-rejected
Domain: UI · Subsystem: authentication

What happened

  • SMTO blocked a save because it couldn't confirm the request came from your current signed-in page. This usually happens when the page is older than your latest sign-in. This change was not saved.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Copy any text you typed but haven't saved. Reloading the page clears text that hasn't been saved.
  2. Reload the page, and sign in again if SMTO asks you to. Reloading gives the page the security code for your current sign-in, which SMTO checks on every save.
  3. Check whether your change is already there, and make it again only if it isn't. This save was blocked, but checking first avoids doubling anything you saved earlier.
  4. If it keeps happening, open SMTO using the exact web address your administrator gave you, not another name or number for the same computer. SMTO only accepts saves from pages opened at its own web address.

What success looks like

  • Your change saves once and is still there after you reload the page.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO, together with the web address you use to open SMTO. Never include your password or browser cookies.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The portal middleware returned csrf_rejected because a state-changing request failed the same-origin check or carried an X-SMTO-CSRF token that doesn't match the current session (or a sign-in POST was not same-origin JSON).

What this means

  • The server could not verify this browser session’s write request. This reports access to the current request, not the outcome of previous operations.

Why this can happen

  • The server could not verify this browser session’s write request.

How to diagnose it

  • The page loads a current session and the intended change saves once.

How to fix it

  • Reload so portal_client.js re-reads /auth/session and its csrf_token, then resubmit after checking current state. If it repeats, compare the Origin header with the URL the Server sees: a reverse proxy rewriting Host or scheme, or opening the UI under a different hostname or port, makes same_origin() fail.
  • Keep unsaved text, reload the page and sign in if asked. Inspect the latest saved state before submitting the change again.

Retry and execution caution

  • The page loads a current session and the intended change saves once.

How to verify the fix

  • The page loads a current session and the intended change saves once.

What not to do

  • Do not delete retained task data or repeat an operation with an unknown outcome.

Technical notes

  • Authentication guidance never changes account permissions or replays task work.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
